title: Tropical Spin-Glass Packet Moves
description: View each defect cluster as a small frustrated spin-glass subproblem and solve it with tropical or min-sum tensor-network methods, while a CA coordinates packet transport and conflict resolution globally. This hybrid preserves local CA structure but upgrades local choices from heuristic flips to micro-optimized packet moves.
mathematical_formalization: For a local neighborhood R, define E_R(p) = sum_{(i,j) in R} J_{ij} s_i s_j + sum_i h_i s_i under packet move p. Compute p* = argmin_p E_R(p) with tropical contraction or min-sum dynamic programming, then let the CA decide which neighborhoods fire and how competing packet moves are merged.
analogical_connections: Exact patch repair embedded in a larger swarm controller.
A min-sum decoder whose variables are packet moves rather than single bits.
Local perfect play inside a globally approximate search process.
implementation_hypothesis: Derive local Ising coefficients from exact Gram-delta formulas, solve only small neighborhoods with a tropical solver, and let the CA schedule those neighborhoods based on defect density and conflict. The micro-solver should improve move quality without sacrificing the CA's parallelism.
experiment_seed: Begin with induced subproblems on order-428 or on controlled defect injections into exact matrices. Compare packet quality and exact repair rate against heuristic packet rules and against full-matrix Ising search.

novelty_claim: The new element is not a global Ising mapping, but exact or near-exact local micro-solves inside a CA defect-transport loop.
differentiation: This is not another simulated annealing or quantum annealing scheme. Only local neighborhoods are solved as spin systems, while the global controller remains a CA.
